Cette tablette d'argile, achetée par Geo: This clay tablet, bought by George Plimpton around 1922, holds a table of numbers satisfying a² + b² = c², a millennium before Pythagoras.
François Viète publie un calcul où les l: François Viète publishes a calculus in which letters replace numbers.
Son Introduction à l'art analytique note: His Introduction to the Analytic Art writes unknowns as vowels and known quantities as consonants. Viète, an adviser to Henri IV, also cracked Spanish secret codes: Philip II accused him of sorcery before the pope.
Publication posthume de l'essai de Thoma: Posthumous publication of Thomas Bayes's essay.
Le pasteur Thomas Bayes n'a jamais publi: The minister Thomas Bayes never published his theorem: his friend Richard Price found it among his papers and had it published two years after his death.
Lobatchevski publie une géométrie où les: Lobachevsky publishes a geometry in which parallel lines behave differently.
Bolyai fait la même découverte de son cô: Bolyai makes the same discovery on his own. Gauss had thought of it without publishing, for fear of “the clamor of the Boeotians”, as he wrote.
George Boole, autodidacte, réduit le rai: George Boole, self-taught, reduces reasoning to calculations on 0 and 1. Claude Shannon would use it in 1937 to design electrical circuits.
Florence Nightingale montre en graphique: Florence Nightingale shows in charts that soldiers die mostly of preventable diseases.
Ses diagrammes polaires, présentés au go: Her polar area diagrams, presented to the British government, helped reform hygiene in military hospitals. She was the first woman elected to the Royal Statistical Society, in 1858.
Georg Cantor montre qu'on ne peut pas nu: Georg Cantor shows that the real numbers cannot all be numbered.
Son travail choque une partie des mathém: His work shocked some mathematicians, including Kronecker. Hilbert would later say: “No one shall expel us from the paradise that Cantor has created for us.”
Francis Galton retrouve la corrélation e: Francis Galton rediscovers correlation by comparing heights and forearm lengths.
Cousin de Darwin, Galton invente aussi l: A cousin of Darwin, Galton also invented the questionnaire, fingerprints in criminology and, unfortunately, the word “eugenics”.
Dans une grotte d'Afrique australe, quel: In a cave in southern Africa, someone notches a baboon fibula.
Entre 42 000 et 43 000 ans d'âge : bâton: Between 42,000 and 43,000 years old: tally stick or ritual object, it is one of the oldest notched objects known.
Un scribe égyptien calcule le volume d'u: An Egyptian scribe calculates the volume of a truncated pyramid, and gets it right.
25 problèmes ; le 14e donne 56 pour une: 25 problems; the 14th gives 56 for a truncated pyramid of 4, 2 and 6. Bought in Thebes in 1892 or 1893, it is in the Pushkin Museum.
À Constantinople, Heiberg reconnaît des: In Constantinople, Heiberg recognises texts by Archimedes beneath a 13th-century prayer book.
Il en tire La Méthode, seule copie connu: From it he recovered The Method, the only known copy. The manuscript, sold again in 1998, gave up the rest of its secrets under X-rays.
Liu Hui commente les Neuf chapitres et c: Liu Hui comments on the Nine Chapters and calculates π with a 3,072-sided polygon.
Il obtient 3,14159, mieux qu'Archimède e: He obtains 3.14159, better than Archimedes and Ptolemy, and attaches a manual for measuring what cannot be reached.
Un paysan trouve près de Mardan un manus: A peasant near Mardan finds a mathematical manuscript in which a dot marks zero.
Conservé à la Bodléienne d'Oxford, il a: Kept in Oxford's Bodleian Library, it was carbon-dated in 2017 with gaps of several centuries between folios; Oxford revised those dates in 2024.
Bombelli donne les règles pour calculer: Bombelli gives the rules for calculating with roots of negative numbers.
« Plus de moins par plus de moins fait m: "Plus of minus by plus of minus makes minus": complex numbers get their rules, and Bombelli solves equations where Cardano had given up.
Henry Briggs fait le voyage jusqu'à Édim: Henry Briggs travels to Edinburgh to meet the inventor of logarithms.
Ils s'accordent sur une nouvelle échelle: They agree on a new scale; Briggs would compute base-10 logarithms, to 14 decimals.
La Royal Society donne raison à Newton c: The Royal Society finds for Newton against Leibniz, in a report written by Newton.
Leibniz n'a pas été entendu et ne découv: Leibniz was not heard and only discovered the text in autumn 1714. Historians today judge the two discoveries independent.
Appel et Haken démontrent par ordinateur: Appel and Haken prove by computer that any map can be coloured with four colours.
1 834 configurations, plus de mille heur: 1,834 configurations, over a thousand hours of computing: Guthrie's question, asked in 1852, is settled by a machine.
Gödel annonce l'incomplétude le 7 septem: Gödel announces incompleteness on 7 September; the next day, Hilbert proclaims "We shall know".
Deux jours, une ville, deux visions des: Two days, one city, two visions of mathematics. Gödel's announcement went almost unnoticed; Hilbert's phrase ended up on his tombstone.
Six siècles après sa mort, Léonard de Pi: Six centuries after his death, Leonardo of Pisa becomes "Fibonacci" in the writing of Guglielmo Libri.
Le surnom abrège filius Bonacci, « fils: The nickname shortens filius Bonacci, "son of Bonacci". In his lifetime he was called Leonardo of Pisa, or Leonardo Bigollo, the traveller.
À Venise, Erhard Ratdolt imprime pour la: In Venice, Erhard Ratdolt prints Euclid's Elements for the first time.
D'après la version latine de Campanus. O: From Campanus's Latin version. It is estimated that only the Bible has had more editions since.
Dans sa Summa, Luca Pacioli donne une as: In his Summa, Luca Pacioli gives a merchant's trick: 72 divided by the interest rate gives the time to double the stake.
À 6 % par an, l'argent double en 72 ÷ 6: At 6% a year, money doubles in about 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years. Pacioli does not explain it: the rule is probably older than him.
À Samarcande, Omar Khayyam commence son: In Samarkand, Omar Khayyam begins his Treatise on Algebra.
Il classe quatorze types d'équations du: He classified fourteen types of third-degree equations and solved them by intersecting conic sections. The poet of the Quatrains was also a mathematician.
